_comment: Splatoon 3 asks for a NAMED matchmaking config and the server decides what it means: how many
players a match needs and accepts. Nintendo configures that server-side, so the game never tells
us — which is why it lives here and not in the code.
Matching is on the LAST path segment, so 'regular' matches tenants/…/matchmakingConfigs/regular.
You will not know the real names until you test: run once, and every unknown config is logged
exactly as the game asks for it. See docs/MATCHMAKING.md.
The counts below assume 4v4 versus modes and 4-player Salmon Run.

configs.name: private
